page: Microsoft Azure EC32ads_v5 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs delivered via an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 192 GB, establishing a 6.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive operations. Local ephemeral storage is bundled as a 1,288 GB solid-state drive (SSD), and the instance supports Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results place the processor and memory subsystem squarely in the average performance tier relative to peers. The EC32ads_v5 recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 2,003.35 and a multi-core score of 34,529.32. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1,217.0 and a multi-core score of 10,136.0, including a Clang software compilation score of 20,796.0. PassMark assessments yielded a CPU score of 32,118.83, an encryption score of 25,385.31, a database operations rating of 12,034.99, and a memory score of 2,196.72. In caching benchmarks, the configuration achieved 29.39 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

Instruction set support includes base AVX, BMI2, ADX, and cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The AMD core configuration does not support AVX-512 extensions or AMX matrix instructions, presenting a tradeoff for workloads reliant on advanced 512-bit vector processing. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of memory paired with 1,288 GB of direct-attached SSD storage, reducing the need for auxiliary disk allocations for temporary files and scratch spaces. The instance fits in-memory caching systems, intermediate database workloads, large software compilation pipelines, and transactional enterprise applications requiring balanced multi-core performance alongside substantial RAM.
description: Microsoft Azure EC32ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor across 16 physical cores. Operating on the x86_64 architecture and virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 192 GB of system memory, maintaining a 6 GB per vCPU allocation. Storage capabilities include a bundled 1,288 GB local solid-state drive alongside support for Premium Storage volumes. Performance benchmarks place the instance squarely within the middle tier for compute and memory operations, registering 34,529.32 on stress-ng multi-core tests, a PassMark CPU score of 32,118.83, and 29.39 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Hardware support includes standard AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions, although advanced AVX-512 vector extensions are not supported. This instance offers a balanced, cost-efficient configuration for mid-to-large relational databases, distributed caching layers, software build systems, and enterprise data processing workloads requiring substantial memory and fast ephemeral storage.
